title: A Hollow for the Wolf
premise: Hazel Blackwood, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, smuggles goods and secrets through the Thornfell mountains until he discovers his own name in a century-old book of prophecies — dated to tonight. Hunted by the crown's inquisitors, he flees into the deep roads where the last dragon, Emberveil, lies guttering in her mountain hollow. Hazel learns that King Aldric has been unmade and replaced by a hollow thing wearing his crown, sustained by stolen dragon-fire, and that the prophecy names Hazel as either the king's unbinding or its final binding. To save what remains of Aldric — and himself — Hazel must speak the forbidden first word of swordspeech, an act that will erase his own name from every memory but one. In the end, Hazel unmakes the hollow king at the cost of being forgotten by all except Emberveil, who carries his true name into the new age.
about_author: C. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and it shows in every treacherous switchback of their prose. They live somewhere with unreliable weather, unreliable neighbors, and excellent tea.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel Blackwood's POV. Smuggling moonsteel over the Thornfell pass, Hazel shelters in a ruined waystation and finds a prophecy book written a century ago — naming him, by name, for tonight. The emotional beat is vertigo: a man whose careful anonymity shatters in a single page.

chapters.title: Inquisitors on the Switchbacks
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Crown inquisitors ambush him on the descent, calling him 'the Swordspeaker' as if they've been waiting a hundred years. He cuts free using oathspeech that answers before he chooses it. Beat: fear curdling into wonder at powers he never trained.

chapters.title: What the Oath Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a flashback to his mentor Vess. He examines the oath-brand on his palm and realizes the words come from the original binding — the same rite that crowned King Aldric. Beat: dread dawning that his gift and the king's curse share one root.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV shift to Sera Vane, court chronicler. In the capital she watches King Aldric sign orders in perfect, lifeless script and notices his shadow moves a half-second late. Beat: quiet horror of a witness no one believes.

chapters.title: Down the Deep Roads
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Fleeing with Sera, who defects with evidence of the hollow king, Hazel takes the smugglers' deep roads beneath Thornfell. The tunnels hum with old dragon-song. Beat: reluctant trust kindling between two strangers bound by the same secret.

chapters.title: Emberveil's Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach the last dragon's hollow: Emberveil, ancient and dimming, her fire siphoned away by unseen channels toward the capital. She recognizes Hazel's brand and calls him 'little word-bearer.' Beat: awe braided with grief for a dying age.

chapters.title: A Century of Borrowed Fire
chapters.summary: Emberveil's POV, rendered as dream-memory. She recalls the pact: Aldric bound a hollow thing into his own body to hold back a greater dark, paying in dragon-fire, and the price has outlasted his will. Beat: tragic context reframing the villain as a wound, not a monster.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Second Reader
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Deciphering the prophecy book, Sera finds marginalia by a previous reader — Vess, Hazel's dead mentor — warning that the prophecy offers two endings and someone has been editing toward the crueler one. Beat: mystery tightening into conspiracy.

chapters.title: Crownfire
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following the siphon-channels, they find a foundry where dragon-fire is forged into the crown itself. Hazel speaks his first true word of power and burns a channel closed; the backlash marks him visibly. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Face
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Summoned back to court, Sera faces the hollow king directly; it knows her name, her doubts, her family. It offers her everything if she delivers the Swordspeaker. Beat: temptation and terror, loyalty tested under a smileless gaze.

chapters.title: Oathbreakers' Market
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Seeking allies, Hazel visits a black market of exiled oath-takers and learns how many have vanished serving the crown. An old rival, Dain, agrees to help — for the prophecy book. Beat: wary bargains in a world where every bond has a price.

chapters.title: Vess's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hidden inside the book's spine, Vess's letter reveals she was the prophecy's original editor — and that she chose the cruel ending to spare Hazel, believing he'd die otherwise. Beat: grief and betrayal entwined; the past rewriting itself.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Emberveil's POV. The dragon teaches Hazel the unbinding: to free Aldric, someone must speak the first word of swordspeech, which erases the speaker from all memory. Emberveil begs him not to. Beat: love and sacrifice laid side by side without resolution.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dain sells their location to the crown; inquisitors storm the hollow. Sera arrives under the king's seal and must choose sides mid-battle. Beat: chaos, heartbreak, and Sera's defection made real in blood.

chapters.title: Chains of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Captured and brought before the hollow king, Sera discovers it is assembling a new body from stolen identities — including fragments of Hazel's. Beat: claustrophobic horror and resolve hardening into a plan.

chapters.title: The Road Back Up
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Wounded and doubting, Hazel climbs toward the capital with Dain's map and Emberveil's fading strength lent as a coal of true fire. Beat: the long dark night of the soul, carried forward by stubbornness alone.

chapters.title: Thornfell Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The mountain itself, saturated with old oaths, responds to Hazel's speech — smugglers' roads opening where none were, the land choosing a side. Beat: belonging discovered; Hazel stops fighting what he is.

chapters.title: The Gilded Audience
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the throne room, Sera stalls the hollow king with chronicles and technicalities while Hazel infiltrates via the mountain's hidden ways. Beat: taut cat-and-mouse, wit as a weapon against something that cannot truly think.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax begins: Hazel reaches the crown and speaks the first word. The hollow thing tears free, wearing a century of stolen faces, and Aldric's remnant flickers within — a man begging to be finished. Beat: terrible clarity at the point of no return.

chapters.title: The First Word
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Full climax: battle atop the collapsing foundry as Emberveil arrives burning her last reserves. Hazel completes the unbinding, offering his name as the price; the hollow thing unravels, and Aldric dies human and grateful. Beat: triumph purchased with self-annihilation.

chapters.title: Everyone Forgets Hazel Blackwood
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aftermath: the kingdom steadies under a regency, Sera writes the true history, and no one can recall the swordspeaker who saved them — only a shape in the smoke. Beat: bittersweet mourning for a man erased by his own heroism.

chapters.title: A Hollow for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Emberveil's POV, closing frame. In the mountain hollow, the dragon keeps a single flame alive — the memory of Hazel's true name, spoken once so it cannot be lost. Somewhere on the roads, a faceless wanderer smiles at nothing. Beat: quiet hope; identity preserved by the only witness who matters.
